description: Reuse the discovery probe's PNGs in /render to avoid the double capture. Today _discover_from_dir runs capture-build.mjs as a probe (first <=20 routes, no --full), reads only the manifest, then immediately deletes the probe dir; /render then re-captures the user's picks with a second capture-build.mjs run. This feature retains the probe PNGs, records a handle-keyed route->PNG map, and makes /render (kind repo/local) reuse a probe PNG for any picked route the probe already captured, capturing ONLY the uncovered picks. Uncovered picks (routes beyond the probe's first-20 window, or picks the probe returned no image for) fall back to a fresh capture, exactly as today. All work stays in backend/routes.py plus its test module; capture-build.mjs is not modified.
steps: In backend/routes.py, add a module-level handle-keyed probe store next to the _JOBS registry, following the existing lock pattern: `_PROBE_CACHE: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}` guarded by a new `_PROBE_CACHE_LOCK = threading.Lock()`. Each entry maps a discovery `handle` to a record: {'dir': <str path to the retained probe dir>, 'routes': {<route str>: <str absolute png path>}, 'created_at': <time.time()>, 'source_mtime': <float | None>}. Add a TTL constant `_PROBE_TTL_SEC` set equal to `_CLONE_TTL_SEC` (3600) so a probe cached at /discover survives to a later /render within the same window the clone survives.

Add helpers mirroring the _JOBS helpers: `_probe_put(handle, dir_path, routes, source_mtime)` (stores under lock, skips if handle is falsy), `_probe_get(handle)` (returns a shallow copy under lock or None), and `_probe_drop(handle)` (removes and rmtrees the retained dir off the event loop caller-side). Keep them small and pure so they can be unit-tested without aiohttp.

Define a `_dir_signature(directory: Path) -> float | None` helper that returns a cheap staleness token for the source directory (e.g. the directory's st_mtime via os.stat, returning None on OSError). This is the staleness rule input: a probe entry is only reused when the current signature of the render target matches the `source_mtime` captured at discover time. Document in a comment that this guards the case where the clone/local dir changed between /discover and /render.

In _discover_from_dir: STOP unconditionally deleting probe_out. Instead, after parsing the probe manifest, build a route->png map from `probe['screens']` entries that have both a 'route' and a 'path' (route string -> absolute path string). If the map is non-empty, RETAIN probe_out and call `_probe_put(handle, str(probe_out), route_png_map, _dir_signature(directory))`. If the map is empty (no usable screens), keep the existing immediate `shutil.rmtree(probe_out, ignore_errors=True)` so empty probes never leak. Update the existing 'probe images are throwaway' comment to describe the new retention behavior and reference the TTL/sweep coordination. Keep `handle` correct: it is the clone_id for repos and 'local:<path>' for local (the same value returned in the response and later posted back to /render).

Coordinate the sweep: in _sweep_clones, dc-probe-* dirs are TTL-swept by mtime already. Ensure a retained probe dir keeps a fresh mtime at retention (touch or rely on creation mtime) so the reuse window is the intended ~1h. ADDITIONALLY, when the sweep removes a dc-probe-* dir, purge any _PROBE_CACHE entries whose 'dir' points inside a removed path so the cache never hands back a route->png path for a directory that was deleted. Do this under _PROBE_CACHE_LOCK. Add a brief comment explaining why (a cache entry outliving its dir would make /render try to serve a missing PNG).

In _handle_render, for kind in ('repo','local') ONLY (url path is unchanged - it uses capture-site.mjs and has no probe): after resolving `directory` and confirming it exists, look up `_probe_get(handle)`. If a cache entry exists AND `_dir_signature(directory)` equals the stored 'source_mtime' (staleness check passes), partition the picks: for each pick whose `ref` is a key in the cached 'routes' map AND whose PNG file still exists on disk, mark it COVERED and reuse the cached path; the remaining picks are UNCOVERED. Build the capture-build.mjs command's --routes CSV from ONLY the uncovered refs. If EVERY pick is covered, skip the capture subprocess entirely and return the reused screens directly (still via a job for response-shape consistency, or synchronously - match the existing job-based response contract by returning {'job': _start_job(lambda: <coro that returns the reused screens>)}). If the staleness check fails or no cache entry exists, behave exactly as today (capture all picks).

Thread the reuse data into the capture step: extend _render_capture_job (or wrap it) so its returned {'screens': [...], 'couldNotSee': [...]} MERGES the reused screens with the freshly captured ones, preserving each pick's original step order (step = pick index + 1) and label. A covered pick contributes {'step', 'label', 'path': <reused probe png>}; an uncovered pick is captured and mapped by route as today; a pick that is neither covered nor produced by the fresh capture goes to couldNotSee, exactly as the current by_route fallback does. Ensure the fresh out_dir (dc-render-*) is still created only when there is at least one uncovered pick to capture, and the existing 'rmtree out_dir when no screens' cleanup still holds.

Preserve all existing synchronous validations in _handle_render (NUL check, field-length check, handle containment check for repos, sensitive-dir check for local, exists->handle_expired). The probe lookup must run AFTER these pass. Reused PNG paths come from the probe dir which was created under uploads by the server, so they need no additional path validation beyond confirming the file exists.

Note the probe/render capture flag difference in a comment: the probe runs WITHOUT --full while /render runs WITH --full (full-page). Reusing the probe PNG for a covered route means that route's image is a viewport (non-full) capture rather than a full-page one. This is an intentional latency-vs-fidelity tradeoff for already-probed routes; document it so a reviewer sees it was considered, and keep uncovered picks on the --full fresh path.

Add tests to tests/test_backend_routes.py following the existing monkeypatch style (patch routes._uploads_dir to tmp_path; use @pytest.mark.asyncio for async tests; use the _Req stand-in). Cover: (a) _probe_put/_probe_get/_probe_drop round-trip and that _probe_get returns None for an unknown/expired handle; (b) _dir_signature returns None on a missing path and a float on a real tmp_path dir, and changes when the dir mtime changes; (c) _sweep_clones purges a _PROBE_CACHE entry when its retained dc-probe-* dir is swept (extend or mirror the existing test_sweep_removes_probe_and_clones_keeps_render); (d) an /render repo/local flow where the probe covered all picks does NOT invoke the capture subprocess (assert routes._run is not called, e.g. via a monkeypatched _run that records calls) and returns the reused PNG paths; (e) a mixed flow where some picks are covered and some are not calls capture-build.mjs with a --routes CSV containing ONLY the uncovered refs and merges reused + fresh screens in original pick order; (f) a staleness-mismatch flow (source_mtime changed) re-captures ALL picks and does not reuse. Validate the tests compile with `python -m py_compile`.

Validate: `python -m py_compile` on both changed files exits 0; `ruff check backend/routes.py` introduces no NEW findings beyond the FEAT-001 baseline count; if capture-build.mjs was touched (it should not be) run `env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --check` on it. State clearly in findings that `python -m pytest` could not be executed in-sandbox and why.
acceptance_criteria: _discover_from_dir retains the probe dir and records a handle-keyed route->PNG map when the probe produced at least one usable screen, and still deletes the dir immediately when the probe produced none.
A module-level _PROBE_CACHE guarded by _PROBE_CACHE_LOCK stores {dir, routes, created_at, source_mtime} per handle, with a TTL equal to _CLONE_TTL_SEC.

_handle_render (repo/local) reuses a cached probe PNG for any picked route present in the cache whose file still exists and whose source signature matches, and builds the capture --routes CSV from ONLY the uncovered picks.
When every pick is covered, no capture subprocess is spawned; the response still follows the existing job-based contract and returns the reused screens with correct step/label ordering.
Uncovered picks (routes beyond the probe's first-20 window or with no probe image) still fall back to a fresh capture, and picks neither reused nor freshly captured land in couldNotSee.
A staleness mismatch (source dir changed since discover) bypasses reuse and re-captures all picks.
The sweep removes retained probe dirs on the same TTL and purges the matching _PROBE_CACHE entries so no cached path outlives its dir.

New pytest tests in test_backend_routes.py cover round-trip cache, staleness, sweep purge, all-covered (no subprocess), mixed reuse, and staleness-mismatch re-capture; all changed files pass python -m py_compile.
ruff check on backend/routes.py shows no new findings beyond the FEAT-001 baseline; capture-build.mjs is unchanged.

findings:
Implemented probe-PNG reuse in backend/routes.py and added tests to tests/test_backend_routes.py. capture-build.mjs was NOT modified.

What changed in backend/routes.py:
- Added module-level _PROBE_CACHE (dict[str, dict]) guarded by _PROBE_CACHE_LOCK and _PROBE_TTL_SEC = _CLONE_TTL_SEC (3600), mirroring the _JOBS registry pattern. Each entry: {dir, routes:{route->abs png}, created_at, source_mtime}.
- Added helpers _probe_put(handle,dir,routes,source_mtime) (skips falsy handle), _probe_get(handle) (returns a shallow copy of a live/non-expired entry or None), _probe_drop(handle) (pops + rmtree; blocking, caller wraps in to_thread), and _dir_signature(directory)->float|None (os.stat().st_mtime staleness token, None on OSError).
- _sweep_clones now records the dc-clones/* and dc-probe-* dirs it removes and, under _PROBE_CACHE_LOCK, purges any _PROBE_CACHE entry whose 'dir' equals or lives under a removed path, so a cache entry can never outlive its dir.
- _discover_from_dir: builds a route->png map from probe['screens'] entries with both route and path. If non-empty it RETAINS probe_out and calls _probe_put(handle, str(probe_out), map, _dir_signature(directory)); if empty it keeps the immediate shutil.rmtree(probe_out). Comment updated to describe retention + TTL/sweep coordination and the probe(no --full) vs render(--full) viewport-vs-fullpage tradeoff.
- _handle_render (repo/local ONLY; url path unchanged): after the existing synchronous validations (NUL, field-length, repo handle containment, sensitive-dir, exists->handle_expired) it calls _probe_get(handle); if a live entry exists AND cached source_mtime == _dir_signature(directory), it reuses the cached PNG for any picked ref whose file still exists (os.path.exists). uncovered = picks not reused. If uncovered is empty it skips the subprocess entirely (no node, no dc-render dir) and returns the reused screens through a job (_reused_only coro) preserving pick-order steps. Otherwise it builds capture-build.mjs --routes=<csv of ONLY uncovered refs> --out=dc-render-* --full and threads the reused map into _render_capture_job.
- _render_capture_job gained a reused: dict[str,str]|None param. For repo/local it emits reused PNGs at each covered pick's original step, maps uncovered picks by route from the fresh capture, and sends unmatched picks to couldNotSee. The finally-cleanup now drops out_dir when no FRESHLY captured screen landed in it (all-reused or empty leaves out_dir empty), keeping the dc-render-* history-reference invariant.

Tests added to tests/test_backend_routes.py (existing monkeypatch/_Req style; each patches routes._PROBE_CACHE to a fresh dict so no global leak): _probe_put/_get/_drop round-trip + unknown/falsy handle None; _probe_get expiry past TTL; _dir_signature None on missing / float on dir / changes on utime; _sweep_clones purges the cache entry when its dc-probe-* dir is swept; /render all-covered asserts routes._run is NOT called and returns reused paths in order; /render mixed reuse asserts the --routes CSV is ONLY the uncovered ref and merges reused(step1)+fresh(step2); /render staleness-mismatch (wrong source_mtime) re-captures --routes=/,/about and reuses no probe PNG; _discover_from_dir retains+caches on a usable screen and drops the dir + caches nothing on an empty probe.
